content: The concurrent use of fostamatinib may elevate the concentrations of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates. It is essential to monitor for toxicities associated with the P-gp substrate drug, as dosage adjustments may be required when administered alongside fostamatinib. Loperamide and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is necessary, as QTc prolongation has been reported with doses of fostemsavir exceeding the recommended levels. Gemfibrozil can increase the levels or effects of loperamide by reducing its metabolism. Although the clinical significance is uncertain, close monitoring is advised. Gemifloxacin and loperamide both increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Gilteritinib and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Loperamide and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concurrent use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Granisetron and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Hydroxyzine and loperamide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Isoflurane and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive P-gp substrates. Itraconazole and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Itraconazole also increases the levels or effects of loperamide through other mechanisms. Monitor ECGs when itraconazole is coadministered with loperamide at doses exceeding 16 mg/day. Ivacaftor increases the levels of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of loperamide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Levo-ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Lithium and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lomitapide increases the levels of loperamide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose when used concomitantly with lomitapide. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of loperamide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions if coadministered with P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce the P-gp substrate dose if needed. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. Loperamide decreases the levels or effects of metoclopramide intranasal through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of metoclopramide intranasal with drugs that impair gastrointestinal motility may decrease systemic absorption of metoclopramide. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effect. Vorinostat and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Loperamide liquid is commonly marketed under brand names such as Imodium and Imodium A-D. It is used to treat sudden diarrhea, including traveler’s diarrhea, by slowing gut movement, reducing bowel movements, and making stools less watery. It is also used to reduce discharge in patients with an ileostomy. However, it treats only the symptoms, not the underlying cause of diarrhea. Overuse or abuse of loperamide can lead to serious harm, including irregular heartbeat or death. Always follow the prescribed dosage and avoid taking it for longer than directed.
